subChunks.title: Alerts, Toasts, and Inline Feedback
subChunks.hookHtml: Feedback components — alerts, toasts, and inline messages — are how your UI communicates the result of user actions. Getting them wrong means users submit forms without knowing if it worked, encounter errors with no explanation, or miss critical warnings. The Tailwind patterns for these components are consistent and learnable in one session.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Alert anatomy (inline, persistent)

/* Base alert structure */
<div class="flex gap-3 p-4 rounded-lg border" role="alert">
  <!-- Icon -->
  <svg class="w-5 h-5 flex-none mt-0.5">...</svg>
  <!-- Content -->
  <div>
    <p class="text-sm font-medium">Title</p>
    <p class="text-sm mt-0.5">Description</p>
  </div>
</div>

Alert semantic variants

/* Success */
bg-emerald-50 border-emerald-200 text-emerald-800
icon: text-emerald-500

/* Warning */
bg-amber-50 border-amber-200 text-amber-800
icon: text-amber-500

/* Error */
bg-red-50 border-red-200 text-red-800
icon: text-red-500

/* Info */
bg-blue-50 border-blue-200 text-blue-800
icon: text-blue-500

Alert with left accent border

<div class="flex gap-3 p-4 rounded-lg
            border-l-4 border-red-500 bg-red-50" role="alert">
  <p class="text-sm text-red-800">Error message here.</p>
</div>

Toast (transient, positioned)

/* Toast container — fixed bottom-right */
<div class="fixed bottom-4 right-4 z-50 flex flex-col gap-2">

  <!-- Individual toast -->
  <div class="flex items-start gap-3 bg-gray-900 text-white
              px-4 py-3 rounded-lg shadow-lg
              min-w-[280px] max-w-sm
              animate-in slide-in-from-bottom-2 duration-200">
    <svg class="w-4 h-4 flex-none text-emerald-400 mt-0.5">...</svg>
    <div class="flex-1 min-w-0">
      <p class="text-sm font-medium">Quest Completed!</p>
      <p class="text-xs text-gray-400 mt-0.5">You earned 500 XP</p>
    </div>
    <button class="text-gray-400 hover:text-white flex-none" aria-label="Dismiss">
      ×
    </button>
  </div>
</div>

Inline form feedback

/* Below an input — success */
<p class="flex items-center gap-1.5 text-xs text-emerald-600 mt-1">
  <svg class="w-3.5 h-3.5">...</svg>
  Email is available
</p>

/* Below an input — error */
<p class="flex items-center gap-1.5 text-xs text-red-600 mt-1" role="alert">
  <svg class="w-3.5 h-3.5">...</svg>
  This email is already in use
</p>

Banner (full-width alert)

<div class="bg-amber-500 text-white px-4 py-2 text-sm
            flex items-center justify-center gap-3">
  ⚠️
  <span>Your subscription expires in 3 days.</span>
  <a href="/billing" class="font-semibold underline hover:no-underline">Upgrade now</a>
</div>

Sable: "Every alert needs role="alert" for screen readers. Every dismissible toast needs an aria-label="Dismiss" close button. The ARIA role 'alert' causes assistive technology to immediately announce the content when it appears — essential for form validation errors that appear dynamically."

storyBeats.speaker: Sable the Illuminator
storyBeats.text: An alert that looks red but doesn't say what went wrong is useless. A toast that appears and immediately disappears before the user reads it is cruel. Build feedback components with precision: colour, icon, title, description, and the right accessibility attributes. Make the UI speak clearly.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a complete alert system with all four semantic variants and a toast:

  • .alert: flex, gap-3, p-4, rounded-lg, border
  • .alert-success: bg-emerald-50, border-emerald-200, text-emerald-800
  • .alert-warning: bg-amber-50, border-amber-200, text-amber-800
  • .alert-error: bg-red-50, border-red-200, text-red-800
  • .alert-info: bg-blue-50, border-blue-200, text-blue-800
  • .toast: flex, items-start, gap-3, bg-gray-900, text-white, px-4, py-3, rounded-lg, shadow-lg, min-w-[280px], max-w-sm

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a complete notification system from scratch: a fixed toast container in the bottom-right corner with three stacked toasts (success, warning, error — each with icon, title, description, and dismiss button), a dismissible banner at the top of the page, and a form with an inline error message below a field. Add all appropriate ARIA attributes. No starter code.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the difference between an alert (inline, persistent) and a toast (transient, fixed position). Why does role='alert' matter for dynamically injected alerts? Walk through the left accent border pattern (border-l-4) for alerts and when you would prefer it over a full background colour.

questions.prompt: A toast notification appears in the bottom-right corner of the screen and should stay visible even as the user scrolls. Which positioning classes on the toast container achieve this?
questions.explanation: fixed positions the element relative to the viewport, so it stays in place during scroll. bottom-4 and right-4 provide 16px offset from the screen edges. z-50 ensures the toast appears above all other content. absolute would scroll with the page content; sticky would only stick within its parent container.

questions.prompt: A form validation error alert is dynamically injected into the DOM when the form is submitted. Screen reader users don't hear the error announced. Which ARIA attribute on the alert element fixes this?
options: role="alert" — causes assistive technology to announce the element's content immediately when it appears or changes
aria-live="polite" — announces changes when the user is idle
aria-describedby linking the alert to the submit button
tabindex="0" — makes the error focusable so keyboard users find it
questions.answer: role="alert" — causes assistive technology to announce the element's content immediately when it appears or changes
questions.explanation: role='alert' implicitly sets aria-live='assertive' and aria-atomic='true'. When an element with role='alert' is added to the DOM or its content changes, screen readers immediately announce its content, interrupting whatever they're currently saying. This is the correct pattern for error messages and important notifications that require immediate attention.

questions.prompt: When should you use an inline alert vs a toast notification for a form save operation?
options: Toast for transient success confirmations ('Saved successfully'); inline alert for persistent errors that need user action ('Email already in use — fix before submitting')
Toast for errors (urgent); inline alert for success (low priority)
Inline alert for all form feedback; toasts are only for non-form operations
They are interchangeable — choose based on aesthetic preference
questions.answer: Toast for transient success confirmations ('Saved successfully'); inline alert for persistent errors that need user action ('Email already in use — fix before submitting')
questions.explanation: Toasts are appropriate for transient confirmations that don't require action — they appear, the user reads them, and they disappear. Inline alerts are appropriate for persistent state that requires user action — a form error must stay visible near the problematic field until the user fixes it. A toast would be wrong for a form error because it disappears before the user fixes the field.
